items.title: Show HN: Ranwhat.com
items.summary: Hi HackerNews, My name is Matija, and I'm building ranwhat.com. It's used for checking if any of your secrets have leaked, and where they leaked. It's mostly aimed at solo devs such as myself, but also at anyone using a coding agent. The tool also checks if your coding agent ran any sketchy commands. This is mostly a "better safe than sorry" feature, so you can tell your Claude or Codex not to run them. The project is open source (MIT) and everything runs locally on your machine. How to install it: pip install ranwhat / uv tool install ranwhat, or brew install MatijaMiki/ranwhat/ranwhat There is a free and a paid plan. Everything local is free; the paid plan is 12€ a month and adds server-side features, which you can read more about here: https://ranwhat.com/pricing All I'm asking for here is feedback, and if you have anything you would want added to the project. Looking forward to answering any questions you have. Best, Matija

items.title: Show HN: Sóþspell, a model-guided walkthrough of a codebase
items.summary: I kept finding myself wanting a way to get talked through the code that a model had created, which led to me making Sóþspell (old English, "Truth Story"). You give it a git repo locally or via URL, and it creates a tour of the repo in a web page, with the aim of it explaining the whole thing. There's also model harness plugins for Claude, Codex, and OpenCode. You give it an API key for whatever model you prefer to create the tour (saved locally or via github), and you can also give it a voice using an ElevenLabs API key. I just pushed a canvas view, which I'm hoping I can make the code navigation a bit more helpful. There's a demo codebase, and you can export tours as JSON. The demo doesn't need any keys to work, it falls back to browser speech if you want to hear that. This is my first real, "big" open source project that I've released, prior to this I'd just contributed stuff. I hope it can be useful to someone! I would love to hear some constructive criticism too, and any suggestions on features you'd like to see. It's MIT licensed, and I'll try to stick around in the comments to answer questions if people want.

Show HN: Tabverse – a free, open-source, with self-hostable server Workona clone
items.summary: Hi, I want to share with you my chrome extension: Tabverse, as it is now passed the reveiw of Chrome Web Store and live at: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tabverse/lffblcippn... Tabverse is a local first workona like chrome extension for managing tabs, with its source open at https://www.github.com/liyu1981/tabverse . In essential it has the core functions workona has, but can operate totally locally, which means it will not need an account nor subscription. The only limit is your local storage spaces so that you can have as many spaces(I call tabverse) as you can. It is open source, so not just your data stays with you, and the tool itself will stay with you in future. Beyond the normal workona features (persisted workspace, load/reload/import/export, note/bookmark/history tools), there are features does require a server. Features like backup/sync, global search on all tabverses, and future collaboration (not yet done), can only be possible if there is a server. I build this part in open too: the server is free to self host and open source in same repo of Tabverse. The tabverse's idea was with me few years ago while I was using Workona and was frustrated with its limitation on free tier (remember was only 5 workspaces), and the missing features of managing multiple workspaces at the same time. Tabverse takes the idea of Workona, and develop further: each window with a Tabverse tab is a workspace, all stored in local storage, and multi windows can have multi Tabverses same time, and can switch fast. There can even be window without Tabverse, so besides work, personal stuff or entertainment will have place to go. As I build this alone, in the middle, almost give up on this project, and luckily AI agents now is there: not only I have a good helper, but also I have a partner I can discuss a bit. So this time the first version starts with v0.7.2. But AI agent can never replace the real need from human on what should be built and what works better, so I want to share with you and listen to your feedbacks early. Please give it a try, and every feedback to me is a gift. Besides the self-hosted option, I host a server at https://tabverse.liyu1981.xyz (yes, the same website of intro and docs), but is invitation only. If you want to help me to test in this early stage, you can login with Google (the only social login I configured :)), and request an invitation there. I will act as soon as I find your request :). But do not worry at all if you only want to use Tabverse locally without a server -- that is the first thing when I was building it. In current version there are also AI features built in, and again do not worry as the AI features is using Chrome's Prompt API, which is totally local, with Gemini Nano (first time will need to download it automatically), nothing send to a server, and you can always turn this on of off in settings. Morden computers with decent memory should work well, but some older computer may suffer (so please turn off). And it is Chrome only. (Honestly, Tabverse currently only support Google Chrome, but not other Chrome based browsers).
